newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan wants deal with India to free fishermen.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan wants deal with India to free fishermen.

text.p: Pakistan said on Friday it was willing to release all Indian fishing boats and their crew seized in its territorial waters if India reciprocates.
"We are ready to release all their boats and crew provided they also release Pakistani boats and crew," Foreign Ministry spokesman Khalid Saleem told Reuters.
"We have told them this is a humanitarian issue and both countries should release all boats and crew without any pre-conditions as a humanitarian gesture," he said.
Pakistani newspapers on Friday quoted the private Fisheries Cooperative Society as saying Indian coast guards had detained 34 Pakistani boats and 233 crewmen from 1993 to January 1997.

Pakistan announced last week it would free 38 Indian children held along with adult fishermen as a unilateral goodwill gesture before talks between top Indian and Pakistani foreign ministry officials in New Delhi from March 28 to 31.
On Thursday, New Delhi relaxed visa restrictions for Pakistani businessmen and journalists, and said Pakistani tourist groups would be allowed to visit India.
Saleem gave a grudging welcome to the Indian action.
"We welcome this, but they are not doing us any favour," he said. "If they want to give any concession, they should give it on contentious issues. We don't even consider this a gesture."

The forthcoming talks between foreign ministry secretaries, or top civil servants, will revive a dialogue that foundered in January 1994 over the disputed territory of Kashmir, of which India controls two thirds and Pakistan the rest.
